Our study shows the potential of the Teach-Back method
as an effective strategy for enhancing breast cancer
knowledge among low health literate women. By actively
involving participants in the learning process, this
approach can empower individuals to make informed
health decisions. However, further research is needed to
explore the long-term impact of the intervention and its
generalizability to diverse populations. Longer follow-
up periods are necessary to assess the sustainability of
knowledge retention and behavior change. Additionally,
measures can strengthen the reliability and validity of
future studies. To maximize the impact of health educa-
tion interventions, it is crucial to address the underly-
ing factors that contribute to low health literacy, such as
socioeconomic disparities and limited access to health-
care. By implementing evidence-based strategies like the
Teach-Back method and tailoring interventions to spe-
cific cultural and linguistic needs, we can improve health
